enhanced_information: Aprepitant, Dexamethasone, and Ondansetron are all effective in managing chemotherapy-induced vomiting. Aprepitant works by blocking substance P, which reduces nausea and vomiting, making it effective in chemotherapy settings. Dexamethasone, with its anti-inflammatory properties, also helps reduce nausea and is commonly used in chemotherapy regimens. Ondansetron blocks serotonin receptors, specifically 5-HT3 receptors, and is widely recognized for its efficacy in treating chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting. Therefore, the correct answer is 'All of the above,' as all three drugs play significant roles in the management of this condition.
